findings.issue: isKnown used substring containment; criterion JavaScript with known skill Java matched (termNorm.includes(normalized(s))), so no gap was reported.
findings.reproduction: match_role with jobDescription 'We require JavaScript for this build' and skills ['Java'] produced gaps: [].
findings.fix: isKnown now uses the existing token-aware skillOverlaps()

findings.issue: Cache discriminator /[-+*/%^]/ missed Unicode × ÷ (and −) that the arithmetic parser accepts; normalizeQuery strips them, so '4 × 2' collided with '4 - 2' cache keys.
findings.reproduction: exprKeyed test on '4 × 2' returned false -> shared cacheKey with a different expression.

findings.issue: 'Looking for a data scientist requiring Python' has no role/position/job marker, so extractRequestedRole returned null and 'data scientist' leaked into explicitCriteria.
findings.fix: extractRequestedRole gained a looking-for/seeking pattern that captures the title and stops at the next requirement marker

findings.issue: LEADING_AFFIRM_RE / LEADING_DENY_RE / LEADING_QUALIFY_RE hardcoded he/she/they; 'Ze is not experienced with Rust' under an AFFIRM-required contract was parsed UNKNOWN and bypassed the stance guard.
findings.reproduction: parseLeadingStance('Ze is not experienced with Rust.', zeKb) returned UNKNOWN (pre-fix).
findings.fix: stance patterns are built per tenant from getSubjectPronouns (cached); also added the missing spaced 'is/are not' denial forms for all pronouns; checkStance threads knowledge through

findings.issue: getSubjectPronouns returned object-form pronouns verbatim; { subject: 'ze' } made prompt interpolation emit 'ze/undefined'.
findings.fix: object form now fills missing fields (object falls back to subject, possessive to object)

findings.issue: CLAUSE_BOUNDARY lookahead and buildCandidateSubjectRe hardcoded it|he|she|they; a configured 'ze' subject clause ('…and ze wrote plugins using Vue') did not split, so Vue was validated as an Atlas project technology.
findings.reproduction: validateProjectTechnologyRelationships('Atlas is a dashboard, and ze wrote plugins using Vue.') pre-fix flagged 'Atlas is linked to unverified technology vue'; post-fix returns [].
findings.fix: CLAUSE_BOUNDARY lookahead and candidateSubjectRe now include the configured subject pronoun

findings.issue: Every colon was a hard clause boundary; rendered project evidence 'Project Atlas: a dashboard. Tech: React' stranded the subject from the Tech: cue, so documented technology evidence did not support the claim.
findings.reproduction: evidenceSupportsTechnologyRelation(['Atlas'],'React','Atlas: uses React for rendering.') returned false pre-fix.
findings.fix: colon removed from the clause split (subjectRe already tolerates a label colon); LABEL_FIELD_RE parses Tech:/Stack:/Skills: value lists against the last established subject; cue-only clauses may inherit the block subject; a leading non-subject label colon is retried after

findings.issue: numberMatches extracted only the magnitude of a signed computed result — 'the result is -1' matched '1' and was rejected number_not_grounded:1 even though the computed fact was -1.
findings.fix: number regex is now /(?<![\w.])[-+]?\d[\d.,]*\b/ — sign captured, but '3-4' still yields 3 and 4

findings.issue: isSubjectRef recognized only he/she/they + object forms; 'What projects has ze built?' treated ze as an unresolved entity instead of the tenant subject.
findings.reproduction: assessPrimaryFacet with ze/zir knowledge returned subject:'ze'; with the fix subject:'Morgan Vale'.
findings.fix: isSubjectRef now includes the configured subject/object/possessive pronouns
